title: DOH needs over P1 billion for El Niño preparedness
summary: The Department of Health said it will need a budget of over P1 billion for operational activities within a six-month period to help it address the ongoing super El Niño.

blocks.text: Commuters shield their heads from the scorching heat while trying to catch a ride in Manila in this file photo from October.
MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Health (DOH) said it will need a budget of over P1 billion for operational activities within a six-month period to help it address the ongoing super El Niño.

“For El Niño preparedness, the DOH has developed a preliminary six-month national health commodity budget proposal amounting to P1.165 billion, covering 46 priority commodity lines across 18 regional planning areas for November 2026 to April 2027,” the DOH said in a report.
The DOH, however, said that the proposal remains subject to technical validation, inventory reconciliation and funding approval.

“Funding for El Niño activities shall be sourced from existing DOH appropriations and health emergency funds including Medical Assistance to Indigent and Financially Incapacitated Patients or MAIFIP (for inpatient services) and other applicable funding sources,” the DOH said in a Department Memorandum recently released.
DOH authorized its Centers for Health Development (CHDs) to realign operational funds and resource augmentation to support surveillance systems during declared heat alerts.

The agency noted that part of its El Niño response plan is water safety and sanitation preparedness now being strengthened, including through assessment of water-testing supplies, hygiene commodities and other essential resources needed to address potential water shortages and associated health risks.

Coordination with CHDs and concerned offices continues to identify priority resource requirements and facilitate timely allocation, replenishment and prepositioning of available supplies, particularly in areas vulnerable to El Niño-related health emergencies.

The DOH is also monitoring readiness of health facilities particularly concerning potential mobilization of health personnel, particularly for the assessment, initial management and referral of patients with heat-related illnesses and other priority health conditions.
